  "content": "# SRS: TinyDB String Document IDs in Update and Remove (v1)

## 1. Purpose and scope
- S-01: "`db.get(doc_id='1')` finds my document fine, but when I pass the same id as a string to `update` or `remove`, nothing happens. No error, no warning, the document is just unchanged."
- S-02: "Passing the int `1` instead of `'1'` works."
- S-03: "My ids come from a web form so they are always strings, and I really do not want to crash on every bad input either - but a silent no-op on a write is the worst of both worlds."
- S-04: "Please make these consistent with `get` (which accepts the string form)."

## 2. Actors
| ID | Actor | Basis | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| ACT-1 | Developer / User | STATED | S-01, S-03 |
| ACT-2 | Web Form Client | STATED | S-03 |

## 3. Constraints
| ID | Statement | Basis | Source | Gate |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| CON-1 | TinyDB version 4.9.0 and Python 3.12 environment | STATED | Issue Body | READY |

## 4. Functional requirements
| ID | Statement | Basis | Source | Priority | Gate | AC |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| FR-001 | The table `update` method shall accept string representations of document IDs in `doc_ids` (or convert/normalize them consistently with `get`) so that update operations succeed when string IDs are passed. | STATED | S-01, S-04 | MUST | READY | AC-001-1, AC-001-2 |
| FR-002 | The table `remove` method shall accept string representations of document IDs in `doc_ids` (or convert/normalize them consistently with `get`) so that remove operations succeed when string IDs are passed. | STATED | S-01, S-04 | MUST | READY | AC-002-1, AC-002-2 |

## 5. Non-functional reqs
| ID | Statement | Basis | Source | Priority | Gate | AC |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| NFR-001 | Error handling and type conversion for `doc_ids` in `update` and `remove` shall be consistent with `get`. | STATED | S-04 | MUST | READY | AC-NFR-1 |

## 6. Acceptance criteria
| AC-id | Requirement | Criterion (given/when/then or measurable) |
|---|---|---|---
| AC-001-1 | FR-001 | Given a table containing a document inserted with integer ID `1`, When `db.update({'x': 2}, doc_ids=['1'])` is executed, Then the document is successfully updated and the returned list contains the matched ID type/value consistently. |
| AC-001-2 | FR-001 | Given a table containing a document inserted with integer ID `1`, When `db.update({'x': 2}, doc_ids=[1])` is executed, Then the document is successfully updated. |
| AC-002-1 | FR-002 | Given a table containing a document inserted with integer ID `1`, When `db.remove(doc_ids=['1'])` is executed, Then the document is successfully removed and the table length becomes 0. |

  "action": "write_file",
  "path": ".autose/artifacts/spec.md",
  "content": "# Spec: TinyDB String Document IDs in Update and Remove

## Source
- GitHub issue #35: "`db.get(doc_id='1')` finds my document fine, but when I pass the same id as a string to `update` or `remove`, nothing happens. No error, no warning, the document is just unchanged. Passing the int `1` instead of `'1'` works. My ids come from a web form so they are always strings, and I really do not want to crash on every bad input either - but a silent no-op on a write is the worst of both worlds. Please make these consistent with `get` (which accepts the string form)."

## Requirements
- FR-001: The table `update` method shall accept string representations of document IDs in `doc_ids` (or convert/normalize them consistently with `get`) so that update operations succeed when string IDs are passed.
- FR-002: The table `remove` method shall accept string representations of document IDs in `doc_ids` (or convert/normalize them consistently with `get`) so that remove operations succeed when string IDs are passed.
- NFR-001: Error handling and type conversion for `doc_ids` in `update` and `remove` shall be consistent with `get`.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given a table containing a document inserted with integer ID `1`, When `db.update({'x': 2}, doc_ids=['1'])` is executed, Then the document is successfully updated and the returned list contains the matched ID type/value consistently.
- Given a table containing a document inserted with integer ID `1`, When `db.update({'x': 2}, doc_ids=[1])` is executed, Then the document is successfully updated.
- Given a table containing a document inserted with integer ID `1`, When `db.remove(doc_ids=['1'])` is executed, Then the document is successfully removed and the table length becomes 0.
- Given a table containing a document inserted with integer ID `1`, When `db.remove(doc_ids=[1])` is executed, Then the document is successfully removed.
- Given `get`, `update`, and `remove` methods accepting `doc_ids`, When string IDs are supplied across all three methods, Then all three methods handle string ID normalization identically without silent no-ops.

## Assumptions and open questions
- Assumption (linked to Q-1): Non-existent IDs passed in `doc_ids` to `update` and `remove` continue to be silently ignored, matching existing behavior for integer IDs.
"
